subject: 305409983B8AE48709C636EE4005F04A
introduction: “Make these separate letters into perfect words.” These prayers were written for communities broken up by persecution, exile or quarrel. They ask that the dispersed be gathered, that hatred be put out, and that the hearts of those who pray be joined so closely that they read as one sentence. Unity is asked for as a gift. Jesus’s last prayer, “that they all may be one”, the Qur’an’s reminder that enemies were made brothers “by His grace”, Ezekiel’s two sticks made one, and the church of Acts “of one heart and of one soul” are the same request and its answer. Jesus’s lament over Jerusalem, “and ye would not”, says what the prayers also know: people can refuse.
questions: Why is unity prayed for and not simply decided on?
“Separate letters into perfect words.” What does that image say about what each person keeps in a united community?
Jesus says “ye would not”. What in us resists being gathered?

outside.why: Unite all that is scattered. Jesus’s prayer for his followers: that they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee.
Make these separate letters into perfect words. The eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee.
Heal the distressed hearts and unite their thoughts. Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
That scattered gathering belongs to Thee. Join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.
A gathering whom Thou hast united through Thy grace. Remember Allah’s favour unto you: how ye were enemies and He made friendship between your hearts so that ye became as brothers by His grace.
Unite those scattered by the oppression of enemies. He shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
I have desired naught but the extinction of the fire of hatred. First be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.
Remove hatred from among them. He is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us.
Unite the hearts of Thy loved ones. The multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul.
Purify the hearts from the mention of aught else. Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation.
Gather Thy loved ones beneath the shade of the Tree. How often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
That He unite us. Frost’s neighbour only says, good fences make good neighbours. Is there a separateness between people that these prayers should leave alone?
God of the world and Creator of the nations. Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us?

shortfall: The forty-four prayers ask one thing, that the scattered be gathered and hearts joined; companions were set where the image changes.
